fix(worker): ensure non-root user permissions for pnpm install in Dockerfile

Add directory creation and permission settings to allow the appuser to create
temporary and store files during pnpm install, preventing permission errors
in the container environment.

feat(workbench): improve LSP WebSocket URL generation for internal hosts

feat(worker): migrate Docker image from Playwright to Alpine with non-root user

- Update Dockerfile to use lightweight node:22-alpine base instead of Playwright image

fix(pdf): add browser launch options for custom Chromium executable path

feat(s3): add support for separate public S3 endpoint configuration

Add optional MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT environment variable to allow
browser-facing presigned URLs to use a different endpoint than the
internal service endpoint. This enables production deployments where
MINIO_ENDPOINT is internal-only (e.g., Docker DNS) while browsers
need a public-facing storage URL.

- Add MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT to environment examples and docs
- Add optional validation in shared constants schema
- Update Docker Compose production template with fallback default
- Refactor S3 client to cache separate public and internal clients
- Update all presigned URL functions (getObjectSignedUrl,
  getPutObjectSignedUrl, getMultipartUploadPartSignedUrl) to use
  public client with MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT fallback

feat(worker): configure Playwright browser path and add Dockerfile test

- Add `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` environment variable to worker Dockerfile and production compose
- Install Chromium explicitly in Docker image for PDF export jobs
- Add test to verify worker Dockerfile configuration
- Update README with production note about Playwright browser path

- Worker now detects when sandbox-runner rejects security scan actions and retries without them

refactor(local-dev): improve preflight script output and command handling

- Modify runCommand to use stdio: "inherit" for direct output streaming

refactor(tests): consolidate vi.mock calls into shared fixture modules

test(web,worker): convert file-based assertions to behavioral unit tests

Convert test suites across web and worker apps from file existence and content assertion patterns to behavioral unit tests with proper mocking.

- Rewrite web tests (audit-compare-core, audits-routes, pdf-route, projects-routes, rate-limit, run-audit-route, ton-lsp-client, workbench-actions, working-copy-file-route, working-copy-tree-route) to use vi mocks and test actual runtime behavior
- Update infrastructure tests (dev-compose, drizzle-migration, lsp-service-dockerfile, root-env-dev-scripts) to parse and validate configuration rather than checking raw file content
- Refactor worker tests (ingest-lifecycle, pdf-template, verify-progress-events) to test processor behavior with mocked dependencies

- Improve test isolation by mocking external dependencies (db, s3, redis, external APIs)

refactor(rate-limit): migrate from in-memory to redis-backed sliding window implementation

Replace in-memory rate limiting with atomic Redis-based sliding window
script to support multi-instance deployments. Update API endpoints to
await the async rate limit check and handle unavailable rate limiter.

Add database migration to enforce single active working copy per

in Dockerfile for reproducibility.

refactor(web): remove auth schema, UI components, and project upload form

This commit deletes multiple files as part of a cleanup or migration effort:
- Removes the entire authentication schema (users, sessions, accounts, verifications)
- Deletes a project upload form component for ZIP and file-set uploads
- Removes 30+ UI component files (accordion, alert, avatar, calendar, etc.)
- Deletes the sidebar component and associated hooks

The changes indicate a significant refactoring where the authentication system, UI component library, and project upload functionality are being replaced or migrated to different solutions.

feat(db): add unique constraints to prevent concurrent audits and working copies

- Add `audit_runs_project_active_unique` constraint to ensure only one active audit per project
- Add `working_copies_active_owner_base_unique` constraint to prevent duplicate active working copies for same user/revision
- Implement conflict handling in upload, working copy, and audit run creation with proper error responses
- Refactor DB operations to use UPSERT patterns for better concurrent safety
- Update job processors to handle unique constraint violations gracefully

refactor(workbench): extract core logic into modular custom hooks

Extract state management and business logic from main TonWorkbench component into three dedicated custom hooks:
- useWorkbenchFiles: handles file tree, editing, and working copy operations
- useWorkbenchAudit: manages audit history, findings, and audit execution
- useWorkbenchEvents: handles backend job event streaming and real-time updates

This modularization improves code organization, reduces component complexity, and enhances testability while maintaining all existing functionality.

refactor(workbench): extract UI components for toolbar and findings panel

Extract inline toolbar controls into dedicated WorkbenchTopToolbar component
and findings panel UI into WorkbenchFindingsPanel for better maintainability
and separation of concerns. Simplify audit history badge display by moving
profile label inline with model and finding count.

- Simplify frontend workbench by removing variant selection UI
- Update database schema and shared types to default to internal variant
- Remove audit flow section from landing page for cleaner presentation
- Enhance PDF template with improved TOC, taxonomy mapping, and publication-ready formatting

feat(pdf): include AI model metadata in audit reports

The `used` field is now stored in the report JSON schema, passed through the audit processor, and rendered in the PDF template alongside primary and fallback model identifiers. Also includes a branded footer and validation tests.

- Pass `usedModel` from audit processor into report generation

feat(queues): escape BullMQ reserved colon in job IDs

BullMQ uses colon as a reserved separator in its Redis keys, which conflicts with our job IDs that may contain colons. Added a utility function to replace colons with double underscores in job IDs before enqueuing to prevent Redis key structure corruption.

All queue job enqueuing functions now use the sanitized job ID to ensure compatibility with BullMQ's Redis key naming conventions.
